title: zazzle run operations
description: `zazzle daemon wrap`, which `zazzle run` reaches by exec (src/macos/zazzle); on Intel Macs, which have no invoker, it is run as `zazzle daemon wrap` directly.

entities.name: zazzle run
entities.description: Runs a command and prints its output cleaned, then exits with the command's code.
entities.transport: zazzle run [--lossless] [--budget T] [--timeout SECS] [--profile NAME|none] [--llm INSTRUCTION] [--] CMD ARGS.. (exec'd as `zazzle daemon wrap ...`)
entities.authorization: Whoever runs it; the command runs with the caller's environment, working directory, standard input and permissions. Nothing else is checked.
entities.result: The command's merged standard output and error, cleaned with its profile (detected, or named with --profile) and clean's steps within --budget (default 8000), then `[exit N in Ts; ...]` naming a timeout, cut output and what the profile dropped. With an output store it starts with `[r:ID]` and, when anything was dropped or cut, ends with `[full output: read-again r:ID --full]`; a store that cannot be written leaves it untagged with `[output not stored for read-again: ...]`. The exit status is the command's: its code, 128 + N for signal N, or 124 when it was killed after --timeout (default 3600 s). With --llm INSTRUCTION, the delivered text goes to the local model with the instruction instead, and the agent gets its answer marked `[post-processed by the local model: ~N → ~M tokens ...]`.
failures: No command, an unknown option, a number below 1 for --budget or --timeout, or an unknown profile name: `daemon: ...` with the usage or the profile names, exit 2.
The command cannot be started: `daemon: cannot run CMD: ...`, exit 2.
The pipe cannot be created: `daemon: cannot create a pipe: ...`, exit 2.
--llm without an instruction: `daemon: --llm needs an instruction for the local model`, exit 2.

With --llm, the local model fails (no model downloaded, timeout, input over 400,000 bytes): `error: REASON; the output as it is:` and then the output, with the command's exit status, since the command already ran.
